privacy.description: Private tools and anonymized signals so you can make better sexual health decisions without exposing personal details.

landing.heroNote: Built for discretion, clarity, and control.
landing.stepOneBody: Use guides and the window-period calculator first. You can get value before building a network.
landing.stepTwoBody: Log updates for yourself in a private account. Nothing is public by default.
landing.stepThreeBody: See anonymized exposure context with timing and degree, not names or identity trails.
landing.valueOneBody: Aggregation rules, delayed refreshes, and server-side calculations reduce re-identification risk.
landing.valueTwoBody: Timing and recency are part of the signal so outdated reports don't look like urgent events.
landing.valueThreeBody: You control visibility, connection lifecycle, and data retention as the platform evolves.
landing.faqQ1: Can someone see my exact STI status?
landing.faqA1: No. Navilla is built to show aggregate exposure signals, not named individual statuses.
landing.faqA2: It means the user entered the status themselves. Verification labels are planned to add confidence context.
landing.faqQ3: Does timing matter in exposure data?
landing.faqA3: Yes. Signals include recency context so a report from years ago is not shown like a current event.
landing.faqQ4: Can I use Navilla without sharing with others?
landing.faqA4: Yes. You can use public tools and your private account features before adding connections.
landing.ctaBody: Use practical tools, track your own health timeline, and add network context only when you choose.
landing.ctaFinePrint: No credit card. Delete any time.

howItWorks.title: How It Works
howItWorks.subtitle: A plain-language overview of how Navilla protects privacy and turns network data into useful health context.

showYou.title: What we show you
showYou.intro: When someone in your network reports a positive health status, you'll see:
showYou.item2: How many people in your network reported it
showYou.item3: The closest degree — how many connections away the nearest case is (1st, 2nd, 3rd)
showYou.item4: Whether the report is recent (last 30 days) or older
showYou.item5: Whether the condition is still active or has been cleared

neverShowYou.title: What we never show you
neverShowYou.intro: Navilla is built so that you can't identify who reported what:
neverShowYou.item1: We never show names, usernames, or emails of people who report a condition
neverShowYou.item2: You can't see which specific connection triggered an alert
neverShowYou.item3: There is no way to browse other people's health statuses

dataSource.title: Where data comes from
dataSource.body1: Today, most health status data is self-reported by users. This means reports can be delayed or incomplete. Verification labels (provider-verified, lab-verified) are planned to add confidence context as integrations roll out.
dataSource.body2: Exposure data refreshes in delayed snapshots instead of real time. This prevents people from adding a connection and immediately inferring that person's private status.

connections.title: How connections work
connections.body1: When you connect with someone and they accept, a confirmed connection is created between you. Connections are stored using cryptographic hashes — not real names or emails.
connections.body2: Your network extends beyond direct connections. If you're connected to Ana and Ana is connected to Luis, Luis is in your 2nd-degree network. This extends up to 5 degrees.
connections.body3: Only confirmed connections count. Pending or denied requests are never part of the graph.

exposure.title: How exposure is calculated
exposure.body1: We build a graph of confirmed connections, traverse outward from you on the server, and group positive reports by condition. You see counts, nearest degree, and timing context.
exposure.body2: If you have fewer than 3 connections, we don't show exposure data at all. With only 1 or 2 connections, an alert could reveal a specific person's status. The 3-connection minimum protects everyone's privacy.

accuracy.title: Accuracy and limitations
accuracy.body1: Exposure signals are useful, but they have limitations you should understand:
accuracy.item1: Exposure does not mean you are infected — it means someone in your extended network reported a condition
accuracy.item2: Exposure does not replace medical advice — use it as a signal to consider testing
accuracy.item3: Data is self-reported and may be inaccurate, delayed, or incomplete
accuracy.item4: The graph only includes Navilla users — your real-world exposure may differ
accuracy.item5: Recency matters — older reports should be interpreted differently from recent reports

whatYouCanDo.title: What you can do
whatYouCanDo.item1: Add connections to build your trusted network
whatYouCanDo.item2: Report, clear, or delete your own health statuses at any time
whatYouCanDo.item3: Remove connections — they'll disappear from your graph on the next refresh
whatYouCanDo.item4: Use exposure data as one input when deciding whether to get tested

dataRights.title: Your data rights
dataRights.item1: View your network size and exposure data at any time
dataRights.item2: Report, update, or delete your health statuses
dataRights.item4: Delete your account and all associated data permanently
dataRights.item5: Request an export of your personal data
